text:
当前ws2812的驱动原本是为了“复用spi”而设计的。但是现在需求改为纯菊花链。
尽管如此，我们的努力并没有白费，当前ws2812驱动确实解决了原先nuttx里驱动的一些时序问题。
所以我的判断是我们自己写的ws2812驱动可以保留，只需要修正注释里的措辞就行

# Project memory

Durable notes for this workspace. DSH has no memory tool, so this directory is
the record and `AGENTS.md` at the workspace root is the router into it.

**Read the topic file before changing the area it covers.**

| File | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [gmac-bringup.md](gmac-bringup.md) | **in progress**: the two wired Ethernet ports — board facts from the vendor DTB, controller facts from the TRM, the completed GMAC clock tree (`rk3576_clk_register_gmac()`), why the `beacon` BSP driver is not the blueprint, the bring-up phases, and what the implemented driver actually does and departs from (it builds; it has never run) |
| [camenc-event-loop-plan.md](camenc-event-loop-plan.md) | **current plan**: converting camenc to one non-blocking `poll()` loop, phases A and B |
| [ethloop.md](ethloop.md) | the TCP loopback test for the two wired ports: why both ends must share a subnet and the client socket must be bound to its port, what it measures, the uniprocessor and IOB throughput limits, and its build registration |
| [nuttx-network-pools.md](nuttx-network-pools.md) | the two network pools that cost days: how they deplete, the `poll_setup()` bug that turns one of them into a blind `poll()`, and how to tell which is short |
| [camenc-zerocopy.md](camenc-zerocopy.md) | the zero-copy arrangement: what it is, that it works, how it was proved, what is still open |
| [camenc-refactor-state.md](camenc-refactor-state.md) | the four-thread model — **superseded by the event-loop plan**; its single-core and scheduler analysis still holds |
| [board-and-build.md](board-and-build.md) | sensor modes, build/flash facts, and the traps that have already cost time |
| [rk3576-vop-stride.md](rk3576-vop-stride.md) | the VOP framebuffer pitch: `REGION0_VIR` is byte-pitch/4, the TRM's RGB888 formula is not, why 720 and 1920 hid the bug, and a configure recipe that still works |

## Earlier memory, not yet migrated

The camenc work was carried by the VS Code GitHub Copilot extension before it
moved to DSH. Its corpus is still on disk, outside the workspace:

```
~/.vscode-server/data/User/workspaceStorage/de62cf27f9b529986a905d9b3ea54d6a/
    GitHub.copilot-chat/memory-tool/memories/repo/
```

Around 130 files, of which the camenc and vepu ones are the relevant set
(`camenc-*.md`, `vepu-*.md`, `rk3576-vepu-*.md`, `rk3576-3a-architecture.md`).
Useful for detail this directory has not yet absorbed, but **treat its mode
indices and code line numbers as stale** — several were already wrong when
checked, and the corrections are recorded in `board-and-build.md`.

19:  * under the License.
20:  *
21:  ****************************************************************************/
22: 
23: /****************************************************************************
24:  * WS2812 addressable LED character driver public interface.
25:  *
26:  * This driver is the kernel-side "upper half" for WS2812-family strips that
27:  * are driven over SPI: each WS2812 bit is encoded as one SPI byte, exactly
28:  * like the in-tree NuttX driver.  Unlike the in-tree driver it keeps no
29:  * pixel shadow buffer and holds no permanent claim on the SPI bus:
30:  *
31:  *   - every write() carries a complete frame and is transmitted
32:  *     immediately, in write() order, with nothing carried over between
33:  *     calls;
34:  *   - the SPI bus is locked only for the duration of one frame, so several
35:  *     strips can share one SPI controller and take turns on it;
36:  *   - an optional select callback is invoked around each frame so the
37:  *     caller can switch an external multiplexer (or do any other work) while
38:  *     the strip is guaranteed to own the bus.
39:  ****************************************************************************/
40: 
41: #ifndef __BOARDS_RK3576_DRIVERS_INCLUDE_WS2812_H
42: #define __BOARDS_RK3576_DRIVERS_INCLUDE_WS2812_H
43: 
44: /****************************************************************************
45:  * Included Files
46:  ****************************************************************************/
47: 
48: #include <nuttx/config.h>
49: 
50: #include <stdbool.h>
51: #include <stdint.h>
52: 
53: #include <nuttx/spi/spi.h>
54: 
55: /****************************************************************************
56:  * Pre-processor Definitions
57:  ****************************************************************************/
58: 
59: /* Pixel representation: one 32-bit word per pixel holding 24 bits of color
60:  * in host byte ordering, 0x00RRGGBB.  This is the same layout the in-tree
61:  * NuttX WS2812 driver uses, so application code can be shared between the
62:  * two.
63:  *
64:  * A write() must carry a whole number of pixels.  It is one complete frame:
65:  * pixel 0 drives the first LED of the chain, pixel 1 the second, and so on.
66:  * Writing a single pixel therefore only programs the first LED, which is
67:  * the protocol's behavior, not a driver limitation.
68:  */
69: 
70: #define WS2812_PIXEL_SIZE 4
71: 
72: /****************************************************************************
73:  * Public Types
74:  ****************************************************************************/
75: 
76: /* Select notification callback.
77:  *
78:  * The driver invokes this callback every time it acquires ownership of the
79:  * SPI bus (the "selected" state), so the caller can perform custom work --
80:  * for example drive the select lines of an external multiplexer that routes
81:  * the shared SPI data line to this strip -- while the strip is guaranteed
82:  * to be the active device.  It is called with select == true right after
83:  * the bus is locked, before any byte of the frame is transmitted, and with
84:  * select == false right before the bus is unlocked.
85:  *
86:  * The callback runs with the SPI bus lock held, so no other WS2812 device
87:  * on the same bus can interleave a frame between the select change and the
88:  * transfer.  It must not call back into the driver or block for long.
89:  *
90:  * It may be NULL to disable the notification (for example while the
91:  * multiplexer hardware is not fitted yet).
92:  */
93: 
94: typedef void (*ws2812_select_cb_t)(bool select);
95: 
96: /****************************************************************************
97:  * Public Function Prototypes
98:  ****************************************************************************/
99: 
100: #ifdef CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV
101: 
102: /****************************************************************************
103:  * Name: ws2812_register
104:  *
105:  * Description:
106:  *   Register a WS2812 character device at 'path'.  The caller supplies the
107:  *   already-initialized SPI lower-half this strip is wired to; the driver
108:  *   does not own the bus and does not configure any pin multiplexing.
109:  *
110:  *   Every write() packs the supplied pixels into a single frame and shifts
111:  *   it out before returning.  There is no buffering: the frame is not
112:  *   retained, and lseek() is not supported (-ESPIPE).
113:  *
114:  *   The SCLK the controller really produces is measured once, at
115:  *   registration, and the bit codes are derived from that measurement
116:  *   rather than from the rate the SPI lower-half reports.  read() returns
117:  *   one text line with that measurement and the codes the last frame used
118:  *   ("freq=<Hz> zero=<bits> one=<bits> rst=<bytes>"), which is how the
119:  *   timing can be checked on a board with no debugger.
120:  *
121:  * Input Parameters:
122:  *   path      - Device node path, e.g. "/dev/ws2812".
123:  *   spi       - SPI lower-half obtained by board code, e.g. from
124:  *               rk3576_spi_initialize(3).  The bus must be dedicated to
125:  *               WS2812 traffic (or multiplexed externally and arbitrated by
126:  *               the select callback): the driver changes its mode, word
127:  *               size and frequency around every frame.
128:  *   select_cb - Optional select notification callback (see
129:  *               ws2812_select_cb_t).  It is invoked with true after the bus
130:  *               is locked and before the frame is transmitted, and with
131:  *               false before the bus is released.  May be NULL.
132:  *
133:  * Returned Value:
134:  *   Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno value on failure.
135:  *
136:  ****************************************************************************/
137: 
138: int ws2812_register(FAR const char *path, FAR struct spi_dev_s *spi,
139:                     ws2812_select_cb_t select_cb);
140: 
141: #endif /* CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV */
142: 
143: #endif /* __BOARDS_RK3576_DRIVERS_INCLUDE_WS2812_H */

2:  * boards/rk3576/drivers/drivers/ws2812/ws2812.c
3:  *
4:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
5:  *
6:  * Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) under one or more
7:  * contributor license agreements.  See the NOTICE file distributed with
8:  * this work for additional information regarding copyright ownership.
9:  * The ASF licenses this file to you under the Apache License, Version 2.0
10:  * (the "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance with
11:  * the License.  You may obtain a copy of the License at
12:  *
13:  *   http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
14:  *
15:  * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
16:  * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT
17:  * WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.  See the
18:  * License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations
19:  * under the License.
20:  *
21:  ****************************************************************************/
22: 
23: /****************************************************************************
24:  * WS2812 addressable LED character driver -- SPI backend.
25:  *
26:  * One WS2812 bit is encoded as one SPI byte, so the SPI clock must run at
27:  * eight times the strip's bit rate.  A frame is bracketed by two runs of
28:  * zero bytes that hold the data line low for the reset/latch time: the
29:  * leading run separates the frame from whatever the line did before it,
30:  * the trailing run latches the frame before write() returns even if the
31:  * data line does not stay low afterwards.
32:  *
33:  * Unlike the in-tree NuttX driver this one never keeps a shadow buffer and
34:  * never holds the SPI bus between writes:
35:  *
36:  *   write()  pack the caller's pixels, lock the bus, notify the select
37:  *            callback, transmit, unselect, unlock.
38:  *
39:  * Consequently every write() is a complete frame and the bus can be shared
40:  * by several strips, each with its own select callback, that take turns.
41:  ****************************************************************************/
42: 
43: /****************************************************************************
44:  * Included Files
45:  ****************************************************************************/
46: 
47: #include <nuttx/config.h>
48: 
49: #include <debug.h>
50: #include <errno.h>
51: #include <stdbool.h>
52: #include <stddef.h>
53: #include <stdint.h>
54: #include <stdio.h>
55: #include <string.h>
56: #include <time.h>
57: 
58: #include <nuttx/clock.h>
59: #include <nuttx/fs/fs.h>
60: #include <nuttx/kmalloc.h>
61: #include <nuttx/mutex.h>
62: #include <nuttx/spi/spi.h>
63: 
64: #include "ws2812.h"
65: 
66: #ifdef CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV
67: 
68: /* This driver exports ws2812_register() with its own signature.  The
69:  * in-tree non-SPI model uses the same name, so refuse to build both.
70:  */
71: 
72: #ifdef CONFIG_WS2812_NON_SPI_DRIVER
73: #error \
74:     "CONFIG_WS2812_NON_SPI_DRIVER also defines ws2812_register(); disable one of the two"
75: #endif
76: 
77: /****************************************************************************
78:  * Pre-processor Definitions
79:  ****************************************************************************/
80: 
81: /* One WS2812 bit is encoded as one SPI byte.  The byte is a run of high
82:  * SPI bits starting at bit 6 (bit 7 stays 0, which also leaves MOSI low
83:  * after the last clock), so the run length sets the WS2812 high time:
84:  *
85:  *   T(high) = high_bits / SPI_clock
86:  *
87:  * The strip decides a bit from that high time alone; the remaining SPI
88:  * bits of the byte are the low time.  The run lengths are derived at run
89:  * time from the clock the controller actually produces, not from the
90:  * requested one: the SPI lower-half can only pick an even divider on a
91:  * fixed set of sources and may land well below the request.
92:  */
93: 
94: #define WS2812_T0H_TARGET_NS 250
95: #define WS2812_T1H_TARGET_NS 650
96: 
97: /* Reset/latch low time.  The part in use specifies RES >= 280 us; the
98:  * shorter 50 us some data sheets quote is not enough here.  The run has to
99:  * be driven, not merely held by the board: once the transfer ends the pin
100:  * is handed back to GPIO, and the strip must already have latched before
101:  * that switch, otherwise the tail of the frame can be disturbed.
102:  */
103: 
104: #define WS2812_RESET_US 300
105: 
106: /* Reset run for the fastest clock the driver accepts (9 MHz), in bytes.
107:  * The transmit buffer is sized for it; the run actually used is computed
108:  * from the achieved clock.
109:  */
110: 
111: #define WS2812_RST_MAX ((9ull * 1000000ull * WS2812_RESET_US) / 8000000ull)
112: 
113: /* One LED is 24 WS2812 bits, one SPI byte per bit. */
114: 
115: #define WS2812_BYTES_PER_LED (8 * 3)
116: 
117: /* Frame layout: leading reset run, up to MAX_PIXELS LEDs, trailing reset
118:  * run.  The leading run re-synchronizes the strip's bit decoder; the
119:  * trailing run guarantees the frame is latched before write() returns,
120:  * independently of how the data line behaves once the transfer is over.
121:  */
122: 
123: #define WS2812_TXBUFSIZE \
124:   (2 * WS2812_RST_MAX +  \
125:    CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV_MAX_PIXELS * WS2812_BYTES_PER_LED)
126: 
127: /* Clock calibration.  The SPI lower-half reports the rate its own model
128:  * derives, and that model and the controller do not always agree: on this
129:  * SoC the TRM's SPI source mux table and the vendor clock tree differ, so
130:  * the reported figure can be off by the ratio of the two sources.  Time a
131:  * burst of zero bytes against the system tick instead and derive the byte
132:  * rate the strip will actually see.  Zero bytes hold the data line low,
133:  * which is the idle state a WS2812 strip expects, so the burst is inert.
134:  */
135: 
136: #define WS2812_CAL_BYTES 2048 /* bytes per calibration burst      */
137: #define WS2812_CAL_MS    90   /* wall time to measure over, in ms */
138: 
139: /****************************************************************************
140:  * Private Types
141:  ****************************************************************************/
142: 
143: struct ws2812_dev_s
144: {
145:   FAR struct spi_dev_s *spi;    /* SPI lower-half owned by the board   */
146:   ws2812_select_cb_t select_cb; /* Optional select notification        */
147:   FAR uint8_t *txbuf;           /* Transmit scratch (not a cache)      */
148:   mutex_t lock;                 /* Serializes write() on this device   */
149:   uint32_t freq;                /* Measured SCLK, 0 until calibrated   */
150:   uint8_t zero;                 /* High-run bit count of the last '0'  */
151:   uint8_t one;                  /* High-run bit count of the last '1'  */
152:   uint16_t rst;                 /* Reset bytes of the last frame       */
153: };
154: 
155: /****************************************************************************
156:  * Private Function Prototypes
157:  ****************************************************************************/
158: 
159: static ssize_t ws2812_read(FAR struct file *filep, FAR char *buffer,
160:                            size_t buflen);
161: static ssize_t ws2812_write(FAR struct file *filep, FAR const char *buffer,
162:                             size_t buflen);
163: static off_t ws2812_seek(FAR struct file *filep, off_t offset, int whence);
164: 
165: /****************************************************************************
166:  * Private Data
167:  ****************************************************************************/
168: 
169: static const struct file_operations g_ws2812_fops = {
170:   .read = ws2812_read,
171:   .write = ws2812_write,
172:   .seek = ws2812_seek,
173: };
174: 
175: /****************************************************************************
176:  * Private Functions
177:  ****************************************************************************/
178: 
179: /****************************************************************************
180:  * Name: ws2812_lock
181:  *
182:  * Description:
183:  *   Acquire the SPI bus and notify the select callback (if any) that this
184:  *   strip is now the active device.  This is the single place where the
185:  *   driver couples to the bus mutex, so every frame is preceded by the
186:  *   callback while the bus is guaranteed to stay with this device.
187:  *
188:  ****************************************************************************/
189: 
190: static void ws2812_lock(FAR struct ws2812_dev_s *priv)
191: {
192:   SPI_LOCK(priv->spi, true);
193: 
194:   if (priv->select_cb != NULL)
195:     {
196:       priv->select_cb(true);
197:     }
198: }
199: 
200: /****************************************************************************
201:  * Name: ws2812_unlock
202:  *
203:  * Description:
204:  *   Notify the select callback (if any) that this strip is about to be
205:  *   deselected, then release the SPI bus.  This is the counterpart of
206:  *   ws2812_lock().
207:  *
208:  ****************************************************************************/
209: 
210: static void ws2812_unlock(FAR struct ws2812_dev_s *priv)
211: {
212:   if (priv->select_cb != NULL)
213:     {
214:       priv->select_cb(false);
215:     }
216: 
217:   SPI_LOCK(priv->spi, false);
218: }
219: 
220: /****************************************************************************
221:  * Name: ws2812_measure_clock
222:  *
223:  * Description:
224:  *   Measure the SCLK the controller really produces, by timing a burst of
225:  *   zero bytes against the system tick while the bus is locked and the
226:  *   strip is selected.  The caller must have programmed the mode, word
227:  *   size and requested clock already.
228:  *
229:  *   The result is only as precise as the tick (about one percent over the
230:  *   90 ms window), which is more than enough to pick the bit codes: the
231:  *   datasheet windows they must land in are tens of percent wide.
232:  *
233:  * Returned Value:
234:  *   Measured SCLK in Hz, or 0 if the measurement is unusable.
235:  *
236:  ****************************************************************************/
237: 
238: static uint32_t ws2812_measure_clock(FAR struct ws2812_dev_s *priv)
239: {
240:   clock_t start;
241:   clock_t elapsed;
242:   uint64_t bytes = 0;
243:   uint32_t freq;
244: 
245:   memset(priv->txbuf, 0, WS2812_CAL_BYTES);
246: 
247:   start = clock_systime_ticks();
248: 
249:   do
250:     {
251:       SPI_SNDBLOCK(priv->spi, priv->txbuf, WS2812_CAL_BYTES);
252:       bytes += WS2812_CAL_BYTES;
253:       elapsed = clock_systime_ticks() - start;
254:     }
255:   while (elapsed < MSEC2TICK(WS2812_CAL_MS));
256: 
257:   if (elapsed <= 0)
258:     {
259:       return 0;
260:     }
261: 
262:   /* One SPI byte is eight SCLK periods, and a tick is 1/CLK_TCK seconds. */
263: 
264:   freq = (uint32_t)((bytes * 8 * CLK_TCK) / (uint64_t)elapsed);
265:   return freq;
266: }
267: 
268: /****************************************************************************
269:  * Name: ws2812_bit_code
270:  *
271:  * Description:
272:  *   Build the SPI byte that encodes one WS2812 bit: a run of high bits
273:  *   starting at bit 6, long enough to represent 'target_ns' at the given
274:  *   SPI clock.  Bit 7 is always 0 so MOSI is low after the last clock and
275:  *   the run never touches the byte boundary.
276:  *
277:  * Input Parameters:
278:  *   freq      - SPI clock actually produced by the controller, in Hz.
279:  *   target_ns - Desired high time, in nanoseconds.
280:  *
281:  * Returned Value:
282:  *   The SPI byte to shift out for that WS2812 bit.
283:  *
284:  ****************************************************************************/
285: 
286: static uint8_t ws2812_bit_code(uint32_t freq, uint32_t target_ns)
287: {
288:   uint32_t bits =
289:       (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)freq * target_ns + 500000000u) / 1000000000u);
290: 
291:   if (bits < 1)
292:     {
293:       bits = 1;
294:     }
295:   else if (bits > 7)
296:     {
297:       bits = 7;
298:     }
299: 
300:   return (uint8_t)(((1u << bits) - 1u) << (7 - bits));
301: }
302: 
303: /****************************************************************************
304:  * Name: ws2812_reset_bytes
305:  *
306:  * Description:
307:  *   Number of zero bytes that hold the data line low for WS2812_RESET_US
308:  *   at the given SPI clock.  One byte is eight SPI bit times.
309:  *
310:  ****************************************************************************/
311: 
312: static size_t ws2812_reset_bytes(uint32_t freq)
313: {
314:   uint32_t bytes = (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)freq * WS2812_RESET_US) / 8000000u);
315: 
316:   if (bytes < 1)
317:     {
318:       bytes = 1;
319:     }
320:   else if (bytes > WS2812_RST_MAX)
321:     {
322:       bytes = WS2812_RST_MAX;
323:     }
324: 
325:   return bytes;
326: }
327: 
328: /****************************************************************************
329:  * Name: ws2812_pack
330:  *
331:  * Description:
332:  *   Expand one 24-bit RGB value into the SPI bytes that shift it out as a
333:  *   WS2812 GRB sequence (the strips expect green first).
334:  *
335:  * Input Parameters:
336:  *   buf  - Location to write WS2812_BYTES_PER_LED bytes.
337:  *   rgb  - Color in 0x00RRGGBB host byte ordering.
338:  *   zero - SPI byte for a WS2812 0 bit.
339:  *   one  - SPI byte for a WS2812 1 bit.
340:  *
341:  ****************************************************************************/
342: 
343: static void ws2812_pack(FAR uint8_t *buf, uint32_t rgb, uint8_t zero,
344:                         uint8_t one)
345: {
346:   uint8_t bit_idx;
347:   uint8_t byte_idx;
348:   uint8_t offset = 0;
349:   uint8_t color;
350:   uint32_t grb;
351: 
352:   grb = (rgb & 0x00ff00) << 8;
353:   grb |= (rgb & 0xff0000) >> 8;
354:   grb |= rgb & 0x0000ff;
355: 
356:   for (byte_idx = 0; byte_idx < 3; byte_idx++)
357:     {
358:       color = (uint8_t)(grb >> (8 * (2 - byte_idx)));
359:       for (bit_idx = 0; bit_idx < 8; bit_idx++)
360:         {
361:           buf[offset++] = (color & (1 << (7 - bit_idx))) ? one : zero;
362:         }
363:     }
364: }
365: 
366: /****************************************************************************
367:  * Name: ws2812_read
368:  *
369:  * Description:
370:  *   Report the clock and the bit codes the last frame was built from, as
371:  *   text, so the timing can be checked on the board without a debugger.
372:  *   There is no pixel state to read back: this is all the device has to
373:  *   say.
374:  *
375:  ****************************************************************************/
376: 
377: static ssize_t ws2812_read(FAR struct file *filep, FAR char *buffer,
378:                            size_t buflen)
379: {
380:   FAR struct inode *inode = filep->f_inode;
381:   FAR struct ws2812_dev_s *priv;
382:   char text[64];
383:   ssize_t len;
384: 
385:   DEBUGASSERT(inode != NULL && inode->i_private != NULL);
386:   priv = inode->i_private;
387: 
388:   nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock);
389: 
390:   len = snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "freq=%lu zero=%u one=%u rst=%u\n",
391:                  (unsigned long)priv->freq, priv->zero, priv->one, priv->rst);
392: 
393:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
394: 
395:   if (len <= 0)
396:     {
397:       return -EIO;
398:     }
399: 
400:   if (filep->f_pos >= len)
401:     {
402:       return 0;
403:     }
404: 
405:   if (buflen > (size_t)(len - filep->f_pos))
406:     {
407:       buflen = len - filep->f_pos;
408:     }
409: 
410:   memcpy(buffer, text + filep->f_pos, buflen);
411:   filep->f_pos += buflen;
412: 
413:   return (ssize_t)buflen;
414: }
415: 
416: /****************************************************************************
417:  * Name: ws2812_write
418:  *
419:  * Description:
420:  *   Pack the supplied pixels into one frame and transmit it before
421:  *   returning.  Nothing is retained for a later call: the frame always
422:  *   starts at LED 0, and each write() carries the whole chain.
423:  *
424:  *   The buffer is an array of 32-bit pixels, 0x00RRGGBB in host byte
425:  *   ordering, and its length must be a non-zero multiple of
426:  *   WS2812_PIXEL_SIZE.
427:  *
428:  ****************************************************************************/
429: 
430: static ssize_t ws2812_write(FAR struct file *filep, FAR const char *buffer,
431:                             size_t buflen)
432: {
433:   FAR struct inode *inode = filep->f_inode;
434:   FAR struct ws2812_dev_s *priv = inode->i_private;
435:   FAR uint8_t *tx;
436:   uint32_t freq;
437:   uint8_t zero;
438:   uint8_t one;
439:   size_t npixels;
440:   size_t rst;
441:   size_t frame_len;
442:   size_t i;
443: 
444:   if (buffer == NULL || buflen == 0 || (buflen % WS2812_PIXEL_SIZE) != 0)
445:     {
446:       lederr("ERROR: write length %zu is not a non-zero multiple of %d\n",
447:              buflen, WS2812_PIXEL_SIZE);
448:       return -EINVAL;
449:     }
450: 
451:   npixels = buflen / WS2812_PIXEL_SIZE;
452: 
453:   if (npixels > CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV_MAX_PIXELS)
454:     {
455:       lederr("ERROR: %zu pixels exceed the %d pixel limit\n", npixels,
456:              CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV_MAX_PIXELS);
457:       return -EFBIG;
458:     }
459: 
460:   nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock);
461: 
462:   ws2812_lock(priv);
463: 
464:   /* The bus may have been used by another strip since the last frame (or by
465:    * a non-WS2812 device on the same controller), so program our own mode,
466:    * word size and clock every time.  Use the clock the controller reports
467:    * back, not the requested one: the encoding below depends on it.
468:    */
469: 
470:   SPI_SETMODE(priv->spi, SPIDEV_MODE3);
471:   SPI_SETBITS(priv->spi, 8);
472: 
473:   freq = SPI_SETFREQUENCY(priv->spi, CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV_FREQUENCY);
474:   if (freq == 0)
475:     {
476:       freq = CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV_FREQUENCY;
477:     }
478: 
479:   /* The figure SPI_SETFREQUENCY() returns is the SPI lower-half's own
480:    * model; prefer the rate measured at registration, which is what the
481:    * strip actually sees.
482:    */
483: 
484:   if (priv->freq != 0)
485:     {
486:       freq = priv->freq;
487:     }
488: 
489:   /* One SPI byte per WS2812 bit only gives usable high times in this range:
490:    * below it the high pulses are too long to be codes, above it they are
491:    * too short to be seen.
492:    */
493: 
494:   if (freq < 3600000 || freq > 9000000)
495:     {
496:       lederr("ERROR: SPI clock %lu Hz outside the 3.6-9 MHz WS2812 range\n",
497:              (unsigned long)freq);
498:       ws2812_unlock(priv);
499:       nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
500:       return -EIO;
501:     }
502: 
503:   zero = ws2812_bit_code(freq, WS2812_T0H_TARGET_NS);
504:   one = ws2812_bit_code(freq, WS2812_T1H_TARGET_NS);
505:   rst = ws2812_reset_bytes(freq);
506: 
507:   priv->zero = zero;
508:   priv->one = one;
509:   priv->rst = (uint16_t)rst;
510: 
511:   memset(priv->txbuf, 0, rst);
512:   tx = priv->txbuf + rst;
513: 
514:   for (i = 0; i < npixels; i++)
515:     {
516:       uint32_t rgb;
517: 
518:       memcpy(&rgb, buffer + i * WS2812_PIXEL_SIZE, sizeof(rgb));
519:       ws2812_pack(tx, rgb & 0xffffff, zero, one);
520:       tx += WS2812_BYTES_PER_LED;
521:     }
522: 
523:   memset(tx, 0, rst);
524: 
525:   frame_len = rst + npixels * WS2812_BYTES_PER_LED + rst;
526: 
527:   SPI_SNDBLOCK(priv->spi, priv->txbuf, frame_len);
528: 
529:   ws2812_unlock(priv);
530: 
531:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
532: 
533:   return buflen;
534: }
535: 
536: /****************************************************************************
537:  * Name: ws2812_seek
538:  *
539:  * Description:
540:  *   Seeking is meaningless for a device that transmits every frame from
541:  *   LED 0, so it is rejected rather than silently accepted (an absent seek
542:  *   method would let the VFS update f_pos, which the driver ignores).
543:  *
544:  ****************************************************************************/
545: 
546: static off_t ws2812_seek(FAR struct file *filep, off_t offset, int whence)
547: {
548:   return -ESPIPE;
549: }
550: 
551: /****************************************************************************
552:  * Public Functions
553:  ****************************************************************************/
554: 
555: /****************************************************************************
556:  * Name: ws2812_register
557:  *
558:  * Description:
559:  *   Register a WS2812 character device at 'path'.  See ws2812.h for the
560:  *   full contract.
561:  *
562:  ****************************************************************************/
563: 
564: int ws2812_register(FAR const char *path, FAR struct spi_dev_s *spi,
565:                     ws2812_select_cb_t select_cb)
566: {
567:   FAR struct ws2812_dev_s *priv;
568:   int ret;
569: 
570:   if (path == NULL || spi == NULL)
571:     {
572:       return -EINVAL;
573:     }
574: 
575:   priv = kmm_zalloc(sizeof(struct ws2812_dev_s));
576:   if (priv == NULL)
577:     {
578:       return -ENOMEM;
579:     }
580: 
581:   priv->txbuf = kmm_zalloc(WS2812_TXBUFSIZE);
582:   if (priv->txbuf == NULL)
583:     {
584:       kmm_free(priv);
585:       return -ENOMEM;
586:     }
587: 
588:   priv->spi = spi;
589:   priv->select_cb = select_cb;
590:   nxmutex_init(&priv->lock);
591: 
592:   /* Measure the clock once, while nothing else is using the bus.  The
593:    * burst is zero bytes, so the strip sees a long low, which is exactly a
594:    * reset; no LED state can be disturbed.
595:    */
596: 
597:   nxmutex_lock(&priv->lock);
598:   ws2812_lock(priv);
599: 
600:   SPI_SETMODE(priv->spi, SPIDEV_MODE3);
601:   SPI_SETBITS(priv->spi, 8);
602:   SPI_SETFREQUENCY(priv->spi, CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV_FREQUENCY);
603:   priv->freq = ws2812_measure_clock(priv);
604: 
605:   ws2812_unlock(priv);
606:   nxmutex_unlock(&priv->lock);
607: 
608:   if (priv->freq == 0)
609:     {
610:       lederr("ERROR: could not measure the SPI clock; "
611:              "falling back to the reported rate\n");
612:     }
613: 
614:   ret = register_driver(path, &g_ws2812_fops, 0666, priv);
615:   if (ret < 0)
616:     {
617:       lederr("ERROR: register_driver(%s) failed: %d\n", path, ret);
618:       nxmutex_destroy(&priv->lock);
619:       kmm_free(priv->txbuf);
620:       kmm_free(priv);
621:       return ret;
622:     }
623: 
624:   return OK;
625: }
626: 
627: #endif /* CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV */

58:  * pull would hold a level), so leaving the pin on the SPI function between

110:  *   SPI3 MOSI in its M0 multiplexing (GPIO3_A1); the SPI3 controller is
111:  *   brought up by the chip driver and shared through the character
112:  *   driver's per-frame bus lock.

115:  *   pin idles as a GPIO output driving 0 and is only muxed to SPI3 while a
116:  *   frame is being transmitted.

2:  * app/ws2812_test/ws2812_test_main.c
3:  *
4:  * WS2812 strip smoke test for /dev/ws2812 (SPI3 MOSI on the KICKPI-K7).
5:  *
6:  * Sequence, all on the first 16 LEDs only:
7:  *   1. red for 1 s
8:  *   2. green for 1 s
9:  *   3. blue for 1 s
10:  *   4. four red, four green, four blue, four white, for 3 s
11:  *   5. all black, then return
12:  *
13:  * Every step is one write() of a complete 16-pixel frame: the character
14:  * driver keeps no state between writes, so the whole frame has to be
15:  * supplied each time.  LEDs beyond the 16th are left untouched (they never
16:  * receive the 24 bits that would update them).
17:  *
18:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
19:  ****************************************************************************/

30:  * Pre-processor Definitions
31:  ****************************************************************************/
32: 
33: /* Device registered by kickpi_k7_ws2812.c. */
34:

    bool "WS2812 addressable LED character driver (SPI)"
    default n
    depends on SPI
    ---help---
        Register WS2812-family strips that are driven over SPI as
        character devices.  One WS2812 bit is encoded as one SPI byte, so
        the SPI clock must be eight times the strip's bit rate.

        Unlike the in-tree CONFIG_WS2812 driver, this one keeps no pixel
        shadow buffer and holds no permanent claim on the SPI bus.  Each
        write() carries a complete frame and is transmitted immediately;
        nothing is carried over between calls and lseek() is rejected.
        The bus is locked only for the duration of one frame, and an
        optional select callback runs around each frame, so several strips
        can share one SPI controller through an external multiplexer and
        take turns on it.

        Do not enable CONFIG_WS2812 (the in-tree driver) for the same SPI
        bus: it locks the bus permanently at registration time.

if WS2812_CHARDEV

    int "Requested SPI clock frequency (Hz)"
    default 6400000
    ---help---
        SPI clock to request, not the strip's bit rate (one WS2812 bit is
        one SPI byte, so the clock is eight times the bit rate).  6.4 MHz
        targets the common 800 kHz parts at 1.25 us per bit.

        The SPI lower-half may not be able to hit the request exactly, and
        the rate it reports back can disagree with the SCLK the controller
        actually generates.  The driver therefore measures the real byte
        rate at registration (about 90 ms of idle low) and derives the 0/1

        MHz is accepted; outside that range write() fails with -EIO.

Good. The in-tree driver exists. So the user's stance: keep our own driver, just fix comments.

Now let me form an honest technical opinion. I should be direct and note where I disagree or where "only comments" understates.

Key analysis:

**1. What was "SPI reuse" in this design?**
Two separate things got conflated:
- (a) SPI as the waveform generator: one bit per SPI byte. That's the same mechanism the in-tree NuttX driver uses. It is NOT about sharing; it's the only way to get deterministic timing without a dedicated PWM/RMT peripheral. This part is unchanged by daisy chain.
- (b) The shared-bus apparatus: no shadow buffer + per-frame bus lock + `select_cb` + "several strips take turns". This was built for multiplexing several strips onto one controller.

The real value that solved the NuttX timing problems is (a) plus three specific things:
- measuring the actual SCLK at registration instead of trusting `SPI_SETFREQUENCY()`'s return;
- deriving bit codes from the measured clock (so divider-rounding can't push T0H/T1H out of window);
- parking the pin as GPIO-low between frames (RK3576 SPI releases MOSI);
- and `rk3576_spi.c`'s fix at line 380-402 (BAUDR write while SSIENR=1 was being dropped) — that fix was *found* because the ws2812 driver called setfrequency per frame. Under a pure daisy chain, if the driver still calls SETFREQUENCY per frame, that bug stays fixed and relevant. If someone later "simplifies" the driver to set the frequency once at registration, the fix stays but the regression test disappears. Worth noting: keep the per-frame setfrequency or at least document why the SPI driver depends on that path.

Actually, that's a genuinely important point: the SPI bug fix is attributed to this driver's per-frame setfrequency. So the driver is also implicitly a regression guard.

**2. Does anything in the code become wrong (not just mislabeled)?**
Let me look hard:
- `ws2812_lock()` does `SPI_LOCK(priv->spi, true)` then calls the select callback. Under daisy chain, the callback is still needed for pin parking. Fine.
- The `rst` leading run: under daisy chain + pin parked low, the leading reset is redundant — but it also covers the case where the very first frame follows board init, and where someone else touched the bus. Keep; it's cheap. But note the cost: 2×300µs per frame, dominating short strips.
- `-EFBIG` for > MAX_PIXELS: fine.
- The `read()` interface: fine.
- One genuine question: **is the per-frame `SPI_SETMODE`/`SPI_SETBITS`/`SPI_SETFREQUENCY` still needed?** Under a dedicated SPI3, yes, because the controller may have been used before (or the mode may not persist across transfers if something else touches it), and it costs three register writes. Keeping it is defensible and cheap; but with a dedicated bus the honest reason is "the SPI lower-half does not guarantee state between transactions" rather than "another strip may have used the bus". This is a comment fix.
- **`ws2812_lock`/`unlock` naming and select_cb semantics**: this is the API surface. In the header, the doc says the callback is for multiplexer control. Under daisy chain it's the pin-parking hook. Renaming `ws2812_select_cb_t` → something like `ws2812_xfer_cb_t` (called with true = data line about to be driven by SPI, false = line released) is worth doing because the name "select" carries the multiplexer story. But renaming is a small, contained change (one typedef, one param, one board callback, header docs, Kconfig text, README).
  - Alternative view: "select" also matches NuttX's SPI `SPI_SELECT()` concept, so keeping the name is defensible. Hmm. Actually there's a subtlety: SPI_SELECT is about chip-select; here the callback does the pin muxing. Keeping "select" invites confusion with CS. But in a pure daisy-chain world, the callback IS effectively "select this strip" conceptually... no, there's only one strip. I'd lean toward renaming to reflect "transfer window", e.g. `ws2812_bus_cb_t` or keeping `select` but documenting as pin handoff. I'll present it as a judgment call and recommend renaming since the docs already mislead.

**3. What the "just fix comments" framing misses:**
- The mux design leaves *structural* traces, not only prose:
  - `select_cb` parameter in the public API (and its doc);
  - the per-frame no-buffer/no-state contract (arguably still right for daisy chain);
  - the README's closing paragraph planning for a multiplexer ("多灯带分时复用同一根数据线要等外部多路选择器硬件就绪后...") — this is a *plan* that is now dead; it must be deleted, not reworded, otherwise it reads as pending work;
  - Kconfig (board + driver) help text with the mux story;
  - `ws2812.c` header block "the bus can be shared by several strips";
  - `ws2812.h` block "several strips can share one SPI controller and take turns";
  - board `.c` "shared through the character driver's per-frame bus lock" / "another strip's frame";
  - `ws2812_test` header comment is fine (it's daisy-chain-aware: "LEDs beyond the 16th are left untouched", which is correct daisy-chain behavior).
- Also: the `CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV` Kconfig note "Do not enable CONFIG_WS2812 (the in-tree driver) for the same SPI bus: it locks the bus permanently" — still true if both enabled; keep but it's about the in-tree driver, not mux.
- And `#error` guard against `CONFIG_WS2812_NON_SPI_DRIVER`: still correct (symbol collision). Keep.

**4. Is there a stronger claim: could we now simplify by dropping the callback?**
The callback exists for two reasons: mux control (dead) and pin parking (live). Could the pin parking move into the SPI driver or board SPI init? Options:
- If the rk3576 SPI driver muxed the MOSI pin itself and did the AF/GPIO switch inside `exchange()`, the callback would disappear. But the chip driver deliberately doesn't own pin muxing ("Pin muxing (SS_N, SCK, MOSI, MISO) is the board's responsibility" — line 36). Verify the claim "the driver solved the timing problems".** Evidence in rk3576_spi.c comment (line 380-402) confirms one concrete timing bug found by this driver (BAUDR write dropped while enabled). And the driver's measured-clock approach is itself a timing fix. So yes, keeping it is justified. I can cite that.

**7. Anything else?** Consider the naming of the config `CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV` and the driver dir `drivers/drivers/ws2812/` — under the repo layout, it's a platform driver. Under pure daisy chain, is a char driver even the right interface? Alternatives: an LED-class (`/dev/userleds`) or a simple library. But the char-dev write-a-frame model matches daisy chain semantics best (one write = one frame = whole chain). Keep. Though note: with a shadow buffer, `write()` of a single pixel... no. Keep no-buffer.

Actually, one more thought: for a daisy chain, the "no shadow buffer" means the app must rebuild the entire frame for every update. For animation that's fine (you build the frame anyway). For a status-indicator use case (change one LED) it's wasteful but simple. Since the frame must be transmitted in full anyway (all LEDs shift), there's no bandwidth saving from a shadow buffer — only app-side convenience. So no-buffer is right. Good, that reinforces keeping the design.

Wait — is that right? On a WS2812 daisy chain, does a partial write work? The strip shifts 24 bits per LED; after LED0 latches its 24 bits, subsequent bits go to LED1, etc. If you send fewer than N LEDs' worth, the remaining LEDs keep... hmm, actually the WS2812 protocol: data shifts through a shift register chain; on latch (reset), each LED latches the first 24 bits that arrived at its position. If you send 1 LED's worth, LED0 gets new data, LED1..N get whatever was in the shift registers — which is the *tail* of the previous frame's data shifted in? No: after a frame of N LEDs, all shift registers hold the last 24 bits for each position. A subsequent 1-LED frame shifts 24 new bits into LED0's register and pushes LED0's old 24 bits into LED1, etc. — the whole chain shifts by one position and the tail falls off. So a 1-pixel write produces a rotation, not a single-LED update. That's exactly what the header's paragraph says: "Writing a single pixel therefore only programs the first LED" — hmm, actually it's subtler: it programs the first LED and shifts everyone's data one position down the chain, so LED1 gets LED0's old value, etc. The header's claim "only programs the first LED" is a simplification that's *wrong* about the rest of the chain in the general case.

Hold on. Let me think about the actual WS2812 internals precisely. Each LED has a shift register with a 24-bit "data in" and "data out". Bits arrive at the first LED, it keeps the first 24 bits, and passes subsequent bits out. On reset (latch), the retained 24 bits are transferred to the PWM output register. So: if a frame carries M < N LEDs, LED0..M-1 get new values, and LED_M..N-1 receive *nothing* during this frame (their shift registers still hold the last 24 bits they retained). What was in their shift registers? Whatever was left from the previous frame's transmission — i.e., after the previous full frame, LED_M's register held the value for position M. So they keep their old values. There's no rotation because each LED retains the *first* 24 bits it sees after reset and forwards the rest; it doesn't shift-in on later bits.

Hmm, but actually each LED's internal register is a shift register: after it captures 24 bits, subsequent incoming bits are forwarded to DOUT, and the capture register is no longer updated until the next latch... Different datasheets model it differently. The common behavior (WS2812B): the first 24 bits after reset are latched into the internal register once 24 bits received; further bits are just retransmitted. On the next reset, the register content is used. So M<N updates LED0..M-1 and leaves the rest unchanged. Yes — the header's claim is right in the common model: the tail keeps its previous value.

OK so the "leave the tail untouched" in ws2812_test is correct.

So: for daisy chain, a partial write is meaningful (update prefix), and no-buffer means the app must supply the prefix each time. Fine.

**8. Is there an argument the user might be wrong?** Yes, one: "keep the driver" is right, but "just fix the comments" risks leaving two live behaviours that were mux-motivated and are now dead weight *or* footguns:
- `select_cb == NULL` "optional" wording;
- the leading reset run (300µs) that only made sense when the line could be mid-something — under daisy chain with pin parking it's redundant; keeping it is fine but should be documented as belt-and-braces, or trimmed;
- the per-frame `SPI_SETMODE`/`SETBITS`/`SETFREQUENCY` triple, whose justification ("another strip may have used the bus since") is now false; the true justification is "state doesn't survive" — that's a doc fix, fine.
- And one *actual* consideration: with the mux story gone, `SPI_LOCK` per frame vs. `SPI_LOCK` around the whole driver lifetime. In-tree driver locks permanently (bad: blocks other SPI users). Our per-frame lock is strictly better. Keep.

I think my conclusion: agree with the direction, with three refinements: (1) the stale wording is in six files, and one of them (README's mux paragraph) should be deleted, not reworded; (2) two items are behaviour/API, not prose — the `select_cb` name/optionality and the reason for the per-frame reconfiguration; decide them explicitly; (3) keep the 3 things that are the actual value (measured-clock bit codes, pin parking hook, per-frame lock) and record why in the comments so a future "simplification" doesn't delete them.

Also worth adding: the SPI driver's `setfrequency`-while-enabled bug fix at rk3576_spi.c:380 is owed to this driver — if you ever stop calling setfrequency per frame, that fix loses its only exerciser. Note it in one place.

Let me also double-check: does the driver still call SETFREQUENCY per frame? Yes, line 473. And rk3576_spi.c's fix is in setfrequency. Good.

Let me quantify the reset overhead to make the point concrete:
- At 6.4 MHz, byte = 1.25 µs. RESET 300µs → 2400 bytes each, total 4800 bytes = 600 µs.
- 16 LEDs: 384 bytes = 480 µs. So reset ≈ 56% of frame. 
- 300 LEDs: 7200 bytes = 9000 µs = 9 ms; reset 600 µs = 6%.
- Frame rate ceiling for 300 LEDs: ~9.6 ms → ~100 fps. Fine.
- For 16 LEDs: 1.08 ms → ~900 fps. Fine.
So overhead is not a real problem; mention only briefly. Actually WS2812_RESET_US=300 because the part in use needs ≥280µs — that's a real constraint, so the trailing reset can't shrink. The leading one could go. I'll mention it as optional.

Now, also worth verifying: is the MAX_PIXELS default 1024 and TXBUFSIZE = 2*RST_MAX + 1024*24 = 2*2700 + 24576 = 29976 bytes ≈ 30 KB kmalloc. Under a "pure daisy chain" with maybe 300 LEDs, 30 KB is overkill but it's heap scratch at init. Could be reduced but not important. Hmm, actually is it worth mentioning? 30KB static-ish heap allocation on an embedded board — notable but it's already there and working. Mention as an aside maybe. Actually if the requirement changed to a fixed daisy chain of known size, the config could be tightened to the real chain length. That's a legitimate "requirement changed" cleanup, not just wording. Good point: MAX_PIXELS=1024 default vs actual chain length. I'll mention it briefly as the one config knob worth re-setting to reality.

Let me check whether there's a decision to be made about pin parking vs. rk3576 spi. Already covered.

Now, should I offer to do the edit? The user asked "你怎么看" — an opinion. I should answer with a clear verdict, the substantive points where I'd go beyond "just comments", and offer to make the changes. I should be concise but substantive. Use markdown, Chinese (user wrote Chinese).

I should not make edits yet — they asked for opinion. Offer.

先说结论：**同意保留驱动**，理由不是“努力没白费”，而是这个驱动解决掉的三个问题都和 SPI 复用无关，纯菊花链一样需要它们。但“只修正注释里的措辞”我觉得略微低估了 —— 有三处要一起处理，其中两处不是措辞，是理由/API。

## 真正值得留的东西（与“复用”无关）

1. **用实测 SCLK 反推 bit code**（`ws2812.c:238` 的 `ws2812_measure_clock` + `:286` 的 `ws2812_bit_code`）。in-tree 驱动是在编译期把 `CONFIG_WS2812_FREQUENCY` 落进几个固定字节常量里的（`nuttx/drivers/leds/ws2812.c:376`），分频器一取整，T0H/T1H 就可能出窗。这个自校准是纯增量价值，菊花链下一模一样需要。
2. **帧间把引脚切回 GPIO 输出 0**（`kickpi_k7_ws2812.c:96`）。这是 RK3576 SPI 控制器传完就释放 MOSI 造成的，和几条灯带完全无关，现在仍然是必须的。
3. 顺带逼出了 `rk3576_spi.c:380` 那个 bug：SSIENR=1 时写 BAUDR 被静默丢弃，源码注释里明确写着“until the WS2812 driver started calling setfrequency() per frame”。**这条要写进驱动注释**，因为它是这个修复唯一的天然回归触发点 —— 谁把“每帧设一次频率”优化成“注册时设一次”，修复就没人跑了。
4. 每帧 `SPI_LOCK`/`SPI_UNLOCK` 而不是 in-tree 的注册时永久占锁（`ws2812.c:382`），这条对单条菊花链也更健康。

而“复用 SPI”真正留下的，只有一整套多路选择器的叙事：`select_cb` 的语义、两处 Kconfig help、头文件、README。

## 三处不是“措辞”的

1. **`select_cb` 的 API 语义**。它的名字和 `ws2812.h:90-91`（“may be NULL … while the multiplexer hardware is not fitted yet”）都在讲 mux。菊花链下它唯一的职责是引脚交接，而 NULL 在这块板子上不是“关掉通知”，是引脚永远停在 SPI 功能上靠 pulldown 兜。建议改名（`ws2812_xfer_cb_t` 之类）并把“可选”改成“本板必需”。这是签名级的小改动，只有一个调用者。

2. **每帧重设 mode/bits/freq 的理由写错了**（`ws2812.c:464-468`：“since the last frame … another strip may have used the bus”）。菊花链下这句是假的；真实理由是 rk3576 SPI lower-half 不保证事务间状态。理由错了，将来就会被当成冗余删掉 —— 正好删掉上面第 3 条的回归路径。

3. **`configs/ws2812/README.md` 末段**（“多灯带分时复用同一根数据线要等外部多路选择器硬件就绪后…”）是**计划**，不是描述。需求变了就该整段删掉，不能改成过去时 —— 留着会读成一个待办。

## 顺带按新需求值得调的两个旋钮

- `CONFIG_WS2812_CHARDEV_MAX_PIXELS` 还是 1024 的默认值，`WS2812_TXBUFSIZE` 因此 **~25 KB**（`2×337 + 1024×24`）。链长定了就按链长设，heap 立刻降一个数量级。

/****************************************************************************
 * WS2812 addressable LED character driver -- SPI backend.

 * One WS2812 bit is encoded as one SPI byte, so the SPI clock must run at
 * eight times the strip's bit rate.  The strip is a single daisy chain: the
 * bytes go out on one wire, and each LED takes the first 24 bits that reach
 * it, re-times them, and passes the rest down the chain.  One frame is
 * therefore the whole chain, first LED to last, and has to be written out
 * in one piece.

 * really produces, not from the rate the SPI lower-half reports (see

 * never holds the SPI bus between writes:

 *   write()  pack the caller's pixels, lock the bus, notify the transfer
 *            callback, transmit, un-notify, unlock.
 *
 * Every write() is a self-contained frame: nothing is carried over between
 * calls and the device has no f_pos-addressed partial update, which is why

/* Transfer notification callback.
 *
 * The driver invokes this callback around every frame, with the SPI bus
 * locked, so the board can get the data line ready before the first bit
 * leaves and settle it after the last one.  It is called with xfer == true
 * right after the bus is locked, before any byte of the frame is
 * transmitted, and with xfer == false right before the bus is unlocked.
 *
 * On this SoC the callback is what keeps the line low between frames: the
 * SPI controller releases MOSI when a transfer ends, so the pad is switched
 * to the SPI function for the transfer and back to a GPIO output driving 0
 * afterwards.  A strip sees a data line left high as a never-ending run of
 * 1 bits and latches white at the next reset.
 *
 * The callback runs with the SPI bus lock held and must not call back into
 * the driver or block for long.
 *
 * It may be NULL, but a board that parks its data line from this hook --
 * this one does -- then leaves the pin on the SPI function between frames
 * and depends on the pad pull to keep the line from floating high.
 */

typedef void (*ws2812_xfer_cb_t)(bool xfer);

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: kickpi_k7_ws2812_xfer
 *
 * Description:
 *   Transfer notification from the character driver.  xfer == true hands
 *   the pad to the SPI function; false hands it back to GPIO, which was
 *   programmed at init to output 0, so the data line stays low until the
 *   next frame.
 *
 *   The callback runs with the SPI bus lock held, so the pad cannot change
 *   state in the middle of the transfer.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static void kickpi_k7_ws2812_xfer(bool xfer)
{
  rk3576_gpio_set_af(g_ws2812_mosi, xfer ? KICKPI_K7_WS2812_MOSI_AF : 0);
}

wiring.  The board glue claims GPIO3_A1 and registers /dev/ws2812; only
the data line is muxed, in its SPI3_MOSI_M0 function (header pin 24, the
one 3.3 V-capable SPI pin on the header).

Between frames the pin is a GPIO output driving 0.  A WS2812 strip latches
on a long low, and a data line left high is decoded as a never-ending run
of ones, which is what turned the whole strip white when the pad stayed on
the SPI function.

The ws2812_test example walks the first 16 LEDs through red, green, blue
and a four-colour bar, then blanks them; each step is one write() of a
complete frame.  It runs on a 4 KB stack because the closing status read
(open/read/printf) does not fit in the 2 KB default.

---
drivers: add the WS2812 SPI character driver

A character-device upper half for WS2812-family strips driven over SPI,
one SPI byte per WS2812 bit.  Unlike the in-tree CONFIG_WS2812 driver it
keeps no shadow buffer and no permanent claim on the bus: each write()
carries one complete frame, the bus is locked only for that frame, and an
optional select callback runs around the transfer so several strips can
share a controller through an external multiplexer.

The bit codes and the reset run are derived at run time from the SCLK the
controller really produces.  That rate is measured at registration by
timing a burst of zero bytes, which is a reset to the strip, instead of
trusting the SPI lower-half's report; read() returns the measurement plus
the codes the last frame used, which is how the timing can be checked on a
board with no debugger.

The 0/1 high times target 250 ns and 650 ns, and the frame is bracketed by
300 us of driven low on each side: the part in use latches on 280 us or
more, so the strip has finished latching before the pin is handed back to
the board.

---
spi: fix the BAUDR write and the SCLK divider model

Two things kept the bus far from the requested clock:

  - BAUDR is only writable while SSIENR is 0.  The driver programmed it
    with the controller enabled, so the divider kept its reset value while
    the parent mux changed; a 6.4 MHz request produced a 250 kHz bus, a
    32 us WS2812 bit.  Disable the controller around the parent switch and
    the BAUDR write, then restore SSIENR.

  - The controller produces SCLK at half of what Fspi_clk/BAUDR predicts.
    With clk_spi3 at 100 MHz and BAUDR=16 a logic analyzer measures
    3.125 MHz, not 6.25 MHz, and the same factor appears at BAUDR=198
    (505 kHz predicted, 253 kHz measured).  Model the divider as 2 * BAUDR
    in both the source search and the achieved-rate report, so
    setfrequency() returns the rate the bus is really running at.

Also record in the clock tree why the SPI mux uses the TRM order: mainline
fixed the same table in 586ff159ec02, while the vendor 6.1 kernel still
carries the older {GPLL/6, CPLL/10, CPLL/20, XIN} order.

证据是 include 图，不是设计意图：

- [ws2812.c](contest2026_062_PharosTech/drivers/drivers/ws2812/ws2812.c) 只含 `<nuttx/*>` 和它自己的 `ws2812.h`；

## 两个真实的残余耦合（都不严重，但你应该知道）

**1. 签名是芯片无关的，执行环境不是。** 回调在持总线锁、`write()` 内部运行，不能阻塞、不能睡眠。它只够表达"拨两下 pad 功能位"这种操作。当初多路选择器方案的真实弱点也在这里：只要 mux 的控制线要经过 I2C IO expander 或任何会睡眠的路径，这个钩子就不成立 —— 这不只是措辞问题，是能力边界。当前纯菊花链用不到，头文件里那句 "must not call back into the driver or block for long" 就是这个边界。

**2. 头文件里混进了一句 SoC 知识。** [ws2812.h:83-87](contest2026_062_PharosTech/drivers/include/ws2812.h#L83-L87)："On this SoC the callback is what keeps the line low between frames: the SPI controller releases MOSI when a transfer ends…"。它写成了 "On this SoC" 所以没冒充通用，但严格讲这是板/芯片事实，放在 `drivers/include/` 里越界。更干净的写法是条件句——"a board whose SPI controller releases MOSI when a transfer ends needs this hook to park the line"——把"哪个 SoC"交给板级文件去说。
